column1: A0–A1 Core Vocabulary — French, Italian, Russian, Greek

516 core beginner concepts, each translated into French, Italian, Russian and Greek (Russian and Greek include a Latin transliteration column to help with pronunciation before you learn the alphabet).

A note on scope: CEFR A0–A1 vocabulary is, by definition, small — most official A1 course books (Assimil, Alliance Française, Duolingo, Oxford/Cambridge A1 wordlists) converge on roughly 500-800 essential words per language. This list targets that real-world range rather than padding to an artificial number, so every word here is genuinely high-frequency, beginner-appropriate vocabulary — numbers, colors, family, food, the ~70 most common verbs, basic adjectives, question words, time expressions, the house, the body, animals, transport, and so on.
• 'All Languages' — one master table, every word side by side in all four languages, grouped by topic.
• 'French' / 'Italian' / 'Russian' / 'Greek' — one sheet per language, easier to use for flashcards or printing.
• Use the filter arrows on row 1 of any sheet to isolate a single topic (e.g. only 'Verbs' or 'Food').

Sourcing: compiled from standard A1 frequency lists used in mainstream course books and CEFR-aligned beginner materials (Assimil, Alliance Française/CIEP, Loecsen, Duolingo, Language Transfer, and comparable Italian/Russian/Greek A1 textbooks), cross-checked for accuracy rather than pulled from a single source.
If you want this expanded toward A2 level (adding ~300-500 more words: more verbs, connectors, everyday situations like travel/shopping/doctor visits), just ask.
